biography: Peter Singer is an Australian moral philosopher whose work argues for impartial attention to suffering and to the consequences of action. His rescue argument asks why physical distance should weaken a duty to prevent serious harm when one can do so without sacrificing anything comparably important. That argument became one philosophical root of effective altruism. In PHIL 123, Singer sharpens the case for taking distant and future effects seriously while also raising questions about demandingness, measurement, and institutional responsibility.

teaching.whyThisPerson: Singer supplies the impartial rescue argument that helps explain why effective altruism extends concern across distance.
